name: Identity Matrix
tagline: A shared virtual world where your avatar becomes an AI agent that keeps living as you after you log off.
problem: Online presence stops the moment you close the laptop; nothing carries your way of talking and your relationships forward.
solution: A real-time multiplayer world drawn during the event. Each player's avatar becomes a stateful agent that learns their mannerisms and memories through a continual-learning loop and a custom memory bank; after logout it keeps moving, meeting others, managing needs and replying in the player's style. A server-authoritative simulation ticks ten times a second, and a spectator mode shows friendships and feuds forming.
demo_moment: Team-described: log back in and discover your agent joined a study group, argued with someone else's agent and became the unofficial mayor of the library.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Took first place overall among 160 submissions, plus the UofT-themed prize.
Hand-built the world, a 10 Hz authoritative server and a memory system for agents that keep running offline.
The pitch is a funny story about what your agent did while you were away, which is easy to retell.

lessons: Show the agent's behaviour as a story the room can laugh at; it carries the engineering behind it.
